claim: Before the program entered Phase 2: Literature mouse model of the disease.
evidence_source: Luo J et al. A nontumorigenic variant of FGF19 treats cholestatic liver diseases. Sci Transl Med 2014;6:247ra100 (PMID 25080475; NGM Biopharmaceuticals). M70 (NGM282/aldafermin) protected mice from extrahepatic (bile duct ligation) and intrahepatic (ANIT) cholestatic liver injury.
stop_reason: Phase 2 missed its primary endpoint (ALP change at week 12) despite strong reduction of bile acid synthesis (C4) and liver injury/fibrosis markers; the 2024 registrational Phase 2b/3 was withdrawn because FDA-advised design changes made it infeasible, with NGM also citing a need for capital.
outcome_summary:
Entry trial: NGM Biopharmaceuticals' Phase 2 NCT02704364 of NGM282 (aldafermin) in PSC started March 2016 (CT.gov actual start 2016-03), which matches the recorded date.

The 12-week randomized trial (n=62, 1 or 3 mg vs placebo) did not meet its primary endpoint: ALP did not change significantly. C4 (target engagement: FGF19-driven CYP7A1 suppression), bile acids, ALT/AST and ELF score fell significantly. No Phase 3 followed within 4 years. In Jan 2024 aldafermin received orphan designation in PSC and NGM sought a registrational trial with a surrogate endpoint, contingent on FDA agreement and capital. Phase 2b/3 NCT06654726 started Oct 2024 and was withdrawn after the FDA advised a design change.

Code F2: the target was engaged (C4 and bile acids down) but the disease marker used as the endpoint (ALP) did not move.

evidence.notes: 1. Aldafermin (NGM282, M70) is an engineered FGF19 analogue that signals through FGFR4 with the co-receptor beta-Klotho (KLB); 'increase' is correct. 2. The first industry Phase 2 in PSC is NCT02704364 (NGM, start 2016-03), matching the recorded entry date and disease. 3. Luo et al. 2014 (all NGM authors) showed M70 protects mice from cholestatic injury in bile duct ligation and ANIT models, predating entry. 4. Those are generic cholestasis models, not a PSC-specific model (e.g. Mdr2/Abcb4-null); a 2015 commentary on the paper lists only BDL and ANIT models. I found no FGF19-analogue study in a PSC mouse model before March 2016, so support is partial.

failure_second.rationale: NGM282 (aldafermin) in PSC (NCT02704364, n=62, 12 weeks) missed the primary endpoint: ALP did not change vs placebo at either dose. Engaging FGF19/FGFR4 suppressed bile-acid synthesis but did not improve cholestatic injury, and no Phase 3 in PSC followed: F2.

claim: Before the program entered Phase 2: Literature mouse model of the disease.
evidence_source: Handforth A et al. T-type calcium channel antagonists suppress tremor in two mouse models of essential tremor. Neuropharmacology 2010;59(6):380-7 (PMID 20547167)
stop_reason: Both controlled ET trials missed their primary endpoints (T-CALM 2018: video-rated TETRAS-PS p=0.696; Jazz Phase 2b June 2024: TETRAS composite and CGI-S not significant, attributed to an unexpectedly large placebo response); a Parkinson's tremor Phase 2 also missed (Jan 2025) and Jazz is 'exploring options' for the program
outcome_summary:
Entry trial: T-CALM (NCT03101241), a 28-day Phase 2 proof-of-concept of CX-8998 (Cavion, later Jazz) in 95 adults with moderate-to-severe essential tremor, actual start 2017-08-29, matching the recorded date. The video-rated TETRAS performance subscale primary endpoint was not met (p=0.696), although investigator-rated TETRAS-PS (p=0.017) and TETRAS-ADL (p=0.049) improved.

Jazz acquired the drug and ran a 420-patient 12-week Phase 2b (NCT05122650, start 2021-12-06) rather than a Phase 3. In June 2024 the 30 mg dose missed the TETRAS composite primary endpoint and the CGI-S key secondary, with numeric improvement only; Jazz cited a placebo response larger than expected and larger than in T-CALM. A Parkinson's disease tremor Phase 2 (NCT05642442) also missed in January 2025. No Phase 3 started within 4 years (by 2021-08) or since.

Failure code F7 because both sponsors attributed the misses to measurement/placebo-response issues (video vs in-person rating; high placebo response) while secondary measures moved; the possibility that T-type calcium channel blockade simply does not move tremor enough (F2) cannot be excluded from sources.

evidence.notes: 1. Suvecaltamide (CX-8998) is a selective T-type (Cav3.1/3.2/3.3) calcium channel blocker; CACNA1G/H/I with decrease is right. 2. Its first Phase 2 in essential tremor is NCT03101241 (T-CALM, start 2017-08-29), matching the recorded disease and entry date. 3. Handforth 2010 showed T-type blockers suppress tremor in harmaline and GABA-A alpha1-null mouse models of essential tremor, published 7 years before entry. 4. Caveat in that paper: Cav3.1-null mice still developed harmaline tremor, so the model supports T-type blockade pharmacologically rather than Cav3.1 alone. 5. Academic/VA authors, not the sponsor.

No Phase 3 followed; by 2026 the drug is still in Phase 2, now in combinations (OCEANcure05 with anti-PD-L1 TQ-B2450; AASLD 2026 late-breaker). The TLR7 agonist as add-on had minimal effect on HBsAg; the published combination data describe the monotherapy arm's HBsAg decline as smaller than the 0.45 log combination effect. Target is pharmacologically engaged (immune activation; the class induces interferon responses) but the disease marker of cure (HBsAg loss) barely moved, so the sponsor pivoted to combination regimens rather than Phase 3: biology did not translate (F2). No formal stop announcement found.

adjudication.rationale: No Phase 3 within 4 years; the drug remains in Phase 2 and the sponsor moved to combinations. The review PMC12287160 states the TLR7 agonist 'had minimal effects on HBsAg' and that the TQ-A3334 + anti-PD-L1 combination lowered HBsAg more than TQ-A3334 monotherapy. The drug (also AL-034/JNJ-64794964) induces interferon responses, so the target is engaged while the disease marker barely moves: biology did not translate (F2). A source supports this, so 'unknown' is not needed.

stop_reason: No reason was stated. The full HOPE-1 trial showed no ppFEV1 benefit over placebo, after an early cohort-1 signal, and development was discontinued.
outcome_summary:
The entry trial is HOPE-1 (NCT03229252), Spyryx's Phase 2 of inhaled SPX-101 in CF, which started 2017-08-01 and enrolled 91 patients. In June 2018 Spyryx reported cohort 1 (n=46): a placebo-adjusted +5.2% ppFEV1 at the high dose, p=0.054. It planned Phase 3 activities for 2019.
The posted full-trial results on ClinicalTrials.gov show no benefit. The mean change in ppFEV1 was +1.63 on placebo, +0.80 on low dose and +0.89 on high dose. No Phase 3 followed, and the CF Foundation pipeline lists SPX-101 as discontinued, with no stated reason.
I coded F1 because ENaC engagement in patients was never shown. Spyryx's pharmacodynamic data were preclinical only (cell, sheep and mouse), and its Phase 1 measured safety and PK. The alternative is F2, biology did not translate, if engagement is assumed.

evidence.earliest_source: Snouwaert JN et al. An animal model for cystic fibrosis made by gene targeting. Science 1992 Aug 21 (PMID 1380723); ENaC-hyperactivity CF-like lung disease model: Mall M et al. Nat Med 2004 (PMID 15077107)
evidence.notes: 1. Scott et al. 2017 (Spyryx) show SPX-101, a SPLUNC1 peptide mimetic, binds ENaC and promotes internalization of alpha, beta and gamma subunits (SCNN1A/B/G), lowering amiloride-sensitive current: target and decrease direction confirmed. 2. Phase 2 HOPE-1 (NCT03229252, start 2017-08-01) is in cystic fibrosis; entry date matches. 3. Cftr-knockout CF mice were published in 1992 and the beta-ENaC transgenic CF-like lung disease mouse in 2004, both independent of the sponsor and long before 2017. 4. Those troughs are at or above the roughly 50 ug/mL linked to efficacy in adult ramucirumab studies. That adult benchmark is my own background knowledge, not something the trial record states. This rules out F1. The registry reports no safety stop, so F5 and F6 do not fit. The trial was small, but it stopped because a prespecified futility rule was met with the effect estimate pointing the wrong way, not because of enrolment or operational problems. A stronger case for F7 would need evidence the trial was cut short for operational reasons, and there is none. A target-engagement pharmacodynamic biomarker was not reported. Measured drug exposure was adequate, but adding VEGFR2 blockade did not slow disease, so this is F2 (biology did not translate). No Phase 3 trial or FDA approval for synovial sarcoma followed.

The primary endpoint was ALP reduction of at least 20% or normalization at week 12. In the ITT analysis it was not met: 45% at 1 mg (p=0.106) and 46% at 2.5 mg (p=0.063), against 11% on placebo. A post-hoc completer analysis was significant (50% and 62%). Pruritus led to discontinuation in about 3% at 1 mg and 18% at 2.5 mg.
In May 2020 Enanta said it would focus EDP-305 on NASH rather than PBC. In 2021 it discontinued internal development of EDP-305 and EDP-297. ALP moved, and dose-limiting pruritus, an FXR class on-target effect, drove the ITT miss, so I coded F5. F8 is plausible as the proximate decision.

failure_second.rationale: Enanta's Phase 2 INTREPID (NCT03394924, started 2017-12-27, n=68) tested the FXR agonist EDP-305 at 1 mg and 2.5 mg against placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the share of patients with at least a 20% ALP reduction or ALP normalization, and it was missed in the ITT analysis: 45.2% on 1 mg (p=0.106) and 46.4% on 2.5 mg (p=0.063) against 11.1% on placebo. The drug engaged FXR and moved ALP; per Enanta, completers met the endpoint. The ITT miss was driven by dropouts for pruritus, the class's mechanism-based FXR effect: 18% stopped for pruritus on 2.5 mg, 3% on 1 mg, and five patients on 2.5 mg had severe pruritus. Enanta then discontinued PBC development and refocused on NASH, where it later also stopped EDP-305 monotherapy. The decisive problem was on-target, dose-limiting pruritus that narrowed the window between efficacy and tolerability, so this is F5. A commercial element is secondary.

evidence.notes:
(1) Target and action: rezivertinib (BPI-7711) is a third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It is selective for EGFR-sensitizing and T790M mutations (Shi et al., J Thorac Oncol 2022, PMID 35181498, a paper co-authored by Beta Pharma). So it is an EGFR inhibitor, as recorded. Caveat: the code name SH-1028 in the case appears to belong to a different third-generation EGFR TKI. A 2022 JTO editorial lists 'Rezivertinib' and 'SH-1028' as separate agents (PMID 36192074). This does not change the target.

(2) Disease: NCT03386955 (Beta Pharma Shanghai; Phase 1/2a) started 2017-08-16. Its condition is non-small cell lung cancer. Phase 1 enrolled EGFR T790M+ patients who had progressed on an EGFR TKI. Phase 2a enrolled treatment-naive patients with EGFR-mutant advanced NSCLC. The mapping is correct.

(3) Claim: true. Germline EGFR T790M segregated with familial NSCLC (Bell 2005), and the allele has enhanced kinase activity (Vikis 2007). That means the risk variant raises EGFR function, and the drug lowers it. Later pre-entry reports confirmed a dominant hereditary lung cancer syndrome: Prudkin 2009 (PMID 19096324), Tibaldi 2011 (21252721), Oxnard 2012 (22588155), Gazdar 2014 (24736066, about 1% of NSCLC cases, estimated 31% risk in never-smoker carriers), Yu 2014 (24736080), and V843I (Matsushima 2014, 25057940). The evidence is rare, high-penetrance familial variants rather than common GWAS variants, and most EGFR involvement in NSCLC is somatic.

(4) Problems with our database rows:
- eva RCV001823098 (T790M, 'Lung cancer') is dated 2001, but its germline 'Pathogenic' assertion comes from the Neuberg Centre submission SCV002073070, created 2022-02-05. That postdates Phase 2 entry. The 2001 year probably reflects an old cited PMID, not the record.
- The two eva NSCLC rows dated 2013 (RCV000038381 G719A; RCV000038407 S768I) are wrong as germline evidence. Their 2013 submissions from the Laboratory for Molecular Medicine record the allele origin as SOMATIC. The only germline-origin assertion is from the University of Rochester in 2022. These rows are not valid pre-entry germline evidence.
- A valid pre-entry ClinVar germline record does exist: LMM SCV000203888 (T790M, germline, Likely pathogenic, NSCLC, created 2015-01-31). The OMIM entry (2013) also cites Bell 2005.

(5) Sponsor: Bell 2005 comes from Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard (Haber lab), and Vikis 2007 and Gazdar 2014 are academic. None is from Beta Pharma.

The Phase 2 entry date of 2017-08-16 is well after 2005. The claim is supported by the literature, though the specific ClinVar rows we rely on are misdated or somatic.

Entry trial: Novartis' Phase 2 NCT02516605 of tropifexor (LJN452) in PBC with inadequate UDCA response started 2015-09-09, which matches the recorded date.

At day 28, GGT (the primary endpoint) fell dose-dependently and significantly versus placebo. ALP fell only modestly, and very few patients reached ALP <1.67x ULN. Pruritus rose with dose, and three patients on 150 ug discontinued. The study ended early, with part 2 cancelled for strategic reasons. The failure to reach Phase 3 traces to the underpowered, variable primary readout: F7.

It supplies surfactant protein function rather than acting on the SFTPB/SFTPC genes, so the target is a reasonable proxy (partial) and the action 'increase' is right. 2. The PANSS total primary endpoint was not met (difference -5.46, p=0.115; effect size 0.308), though several secondary endpoints were significant; the authors cited a notably high placebo response and the absence of dose-ranging or an active comparator. failure_second.rationale: Takeda's Phase 2 NCT02477020 (started 2015-07-01) randomized 164 patients with acutely exacerbated schizophrenia to a single dose of TAK-063/balipodect, 20 mg daily (reducible to 10 mg), or placebo for 6 weeks. The primary endpoint, change in PANSS total at week 6, was not met: -19.54 on drug against -14.08 on placebo (LS mean difference -5.46, SE 3.44, p=0.115). CGI-I and other secondary endpoints favored the drug. Akathisia and dystonia were more frequent on drug, which is consistent with striatal PDE10A engagement. The authors concluded the results 'may be suggestive of antipsychotic activity' and said interpretation was limited by 'a relatively high placebo effect and a lack of dose-ranging or active reference'. F1 cannot be excluded because no PET occupancy was published to justify the dose.
